questions.question: What distinguishes an experiment from an observational study?
choices: An experiment must survey an entire population
An experiment cannot record numerical outcomes
An experiment assigns a treatment or condition
An experiment always occurs outdoors

questions.question: What is the purpose of random assignment in an experiment?
choices: To guarantee a representative population sample
To reduce systematic group differences before treatments
To make all outcomes identical
To choose the treatment with the highest score

questions.question: What is a control group?
choices: A comparison group used to assess the treatment's effect
A group whose results are discarded
A group consisting only of researchers
The group with the largest outcome by definition

questions.question: A diet study compares only teenagers on diet A with only adults on diet B. Which factor is confounded with diet assignment?
choices: The shared measurement unit
The recorded health outcome
The common observation date
Age group

questions.question: What is a placebo?
choices: The strongest active treatment
A measure of sample size
An inactive treatment used for comparison
A random sampling method

questions.question: What does replication mean in an experimental design?
choices: Using only one unit per treatment
Applying conditions to multiple experimental units or repeating trials appropriately
Changing the response definition after seeing results
Copying the same recorded value into every row

questions.question: What is the response variable?
choices: The outcome measured to assess treatment effects
The label used to randomize assignments
The fixed number of researchers
Every background characteristic

questions.question: Why can volunteers in an observational study limit generalization?
choices: Volunteers cannot produce numerical data
Volunteer groups always contain the whole population
Generalization never depends on selection
They may differ systematically from people who did not volunteer

questions.question: Students are randomly assigned to two study methods before taking the same test. What is the treatment variable?
choices: The test score
The students' names
The assigned study method
The number of test questions

questions.question: In an experiment comparing two study methods, why should both groups take the same test under similar conditions?
choices: To ensure every student earns the same score
To avoid differences in testing conditions confounding the comparison
To eliminate the need for assignment
To guarantee the new method works

questions.question: What is the purpose of blinding participants to treatment labels when practical?
choices: To reduce expectation-related changes in behavior or reporting
To prevent researchers from measuring outcomes
To eliminate all random variation
To make the sample larger

questions.question: What is a randomized block design?
choices: Assigning every member of a group the same treatment without randomization
Selecting only units with identical outcomes
Discarding groups that disagree with the hypothesis
Grouping similar units first, then randomizing treatments within each group

questions.question: Why can matched-pairs designs be useful?
choices: They guarantee that every pair has the same response
They avoid all random assignment
They compare treatments within the same unit or closely matched pairs
They require twice as many distinct treatments as units

questions.question: Which design most directly supports causal inference when well conducted?
choices: A voluntary opinion poll
A randomized controlled experiment
A comparison of unrelated historical averages
A single observed success story

questions.question: Why should a study's response measure be defined before results are examined?
choices: It reduces selective choice of outcomes after seeing data
It forces every hypothesis to be accepted
It makes measurement error impossible
It removes the need for a comparison group

questions.question: A school gives a new program only to already high-achieving students, then compares them with others. What is the key concern?
choices: Random assignment made the groups too similar
The response variable cannot be measured
The sample is too large to analyze
Prior achievement is confounded with program assignment

questions.question: A coin flip assigns each participant to one of two treatments. Which issue does this address most directly?
choices: Population coverage bias
Every measurement error
Treatment allocation bias
The need for an outcome variable

questions.question: A study randomly samples residents but lets each choose a treatment. Which claim needs caution?
choices: A description of the sampled residents' choices
A causal claim, because treatment was not randomly assigned
A count of the residents in the sample
A statement that a random sample was used

questions.question: In a crossover study, every participant receives both conditions. Why might their order be randomized?
choices: Order or carryover effects could influence results
Random order makes the two conditions identical
Every participant must receive only one condition
Random order removes the need to measure responses

questions.question: A well-conducted randomized experiment finds different average outcomes between treatments. What should be assessed before concluding the treatment has an effect?
choices: Whether the larger average automatically proves causation without uncertainty
Whether every participant showed an identical response
Whether the treatment-group mean equals the population mean
Whether the difference is larger than expected from chance variation
